organization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine
text: Pigmentation means coloring. Skin pigmentation disorders affect skin color. Melanin is the pigment that contributes to skin color, and changes affecting melanin production can affect patches of skin or larger areas.
title: Skin Pigmentation Disorders

organization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine
text: Too much melanin can make skin darker, while too little can make skin lighter. The MedlinePlus topic page notes that sun exposure, pregnancy, and some conditions can be associated with darker skin, while infections, blisters, and burns can be associated with lighter skin. This source is contextual information about visible pigmentation; it is not a method for identifying a condition from an image or feature value.
title: Skin Pigmentation Disorders

organization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine
text: Patchy skin color describes irregular lighter or darker areas. The MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia describes mottling as a patchy appearance related to blood vessel changes.
title: Patchy skin color
topic: patchy color, vascular appearance, and inflammation context

organization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine
text: The source notes that irregular color can be associated with melanin changes, blood vessel changes, or inflammation related to rashes. It advises contacting a health professional for lasting skin color changes without a known cause, a new mole or growth, or an existing growth that changes color, size, or appearance. These are general source-context statements and do not establish what any SpectraDerm feature or score means.
title: Patchy skin color

text: The American Academy of Dermatology explains that dark spots and patches can occur when something triggers extra melanin production. Its page gives examples including a pimple or psoriasis patch clearing, healing after an injury, certain medicines, irritation from a skin or hair-care product, and hormonal changes.
title: How to fade dark spots in darker skin tones

text: The page describes post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation as one cause of dark spots. It also emphasizes finding the cause of dark spots or patches. This is limited appearance context from the cited source; it is not a diagnostic label or an inference from RGB-derived or estimated spectral features.
title: How to fade dark spots in darker skin tones

text: The American Academy of Dermatology states that rosacea signs can include easy flushing, facial redness on lighter skin tones or brown/violet color on darker skin tones, acne-like breakouts, and visible blood vessels. The page also describes burning, stinging, dryness, rough or scaly skin, and itch as possible experiences.
title: Rosacea: Signs and symptoms

text: The source says visible color can appear differently across skin tones and that blood vessels can be difficult to see on darker skin tones. This limited common-condition context is retained only for later evidence retrieval. It does not mean a visible feature, change score, or estimated spectrum detects rosacea.
title: Rosacea: Signs and symptoms

text: The American Academy of Dermatology describes atopic dermatitis symptoms including itch, dry or scaly areas, rash, and, in some cases, bumps that can ooze or crust after scratching. The page explains that appearance can vary with age and skin tone.
title: Eczema types: Atopic dermatitis symptoms

text: This source supplies limited context about visible surface and inflammation-related appearance only. It does not support determining atopic dermatitis, inflammation, or severity from SpectraDerm features, images, or a change score.
title: Eczema types: Atopic dermatitis symptoms

text: The American Academy of Dermatology lists whiteheads, blackheads, pimples, nodules, and cysts among acne breakouts. Its page describes a whitehead as a raised white or flesh-colored blemish that can form when oil and dead skin cells plug a pore.
title: Acne: Signs and symptoms

text: The source explains that a nodule or cyst can develop when inflammation goes deep into the skin and may feel tender or painful. This is limited common-condition context for later retrieval. It does not create an acne label from an image, a feature value, estimated spectral information, or a Change/Anomaly Score.
title: Acne: Signs and symptoms

text: The NHS states that a new mole or a change in an existing mole may be a sign of melanoma and advises checking skin for unusual changes. Its page describes the ABCDE approach as an aid to noticing asymmetry, border, colour, diameter, and evolving change.
